title: Verify: rejectExecution unit tests with mocked fetch
summary: Unit tests prove rejectExecution sends POST to the reject endpoint with Bearer token and surfaces ApiError.
description: Add tests in game/frontend/tests/executions.test.ts using a stubbed global fetch. The fixture is executionFixture from tests/fixtures/api.ts, which mirrors execution.Execution in backend/internal/execution/execution.go.
acceptance_criteria: Given token 'tok' and id 'exec-1', when rejectExecution runs, then fetch is called once with URL /api/v1/admin/executions/exec-1/reject, method POST and Bearer tok.
Given a 200 response carrying executionFixture, when it resolves, then the result equals executionFixture.
Given a 401 response, when it runs, then it rejects with ApiError status 401.
technical_constraints: Mock fetch with vi.stubGlobal and restore it in afterEach.

steps.action: Add rejectExecution to the named import from '../src/api/client'.
steps.command: cd game/frontend && npx vitest run tests/executions.test.ts
steps.expected: File compiles with the new import and the existing tests still pass.

steps.action: Add describe('rejectExecution') with afterEach vi.unstubAllGlobals(). Test 1 stubs fetch to resolve new Response(JSON.stringify(executionFixture), {status: 200}), calls rejectExecution('tok','exec-1'), asserts the result toEqual executionFixture, fetch called once, URL '/api/v1/admin/executions/exec-1/reject', init.method 'POST' and Authorization header 'Bearer tok'. Test 2 stubs a 401 Response, awaits rejectExecution('bad','exec-1').catch(e => e), and asserts instanceof ApiError with status 401. The fixture comes from tests/fixtures/api.ts executionFixture, matching execution.Execution in backend/internal/execution/execution.go.
steps.command: cd game/frontend && npx vitest run tests/executions.test.ts -t rejectExecution
